order_note: No release-engine predecessor and no ordering constraint. SQL 127 replaces two of SQL 83's functions (aws/workflows/sql/83_homeowner_signing_capabilities.sql, applied to production and retired on its own homeowner engine, so it is not a release key) and adds a third beside SQL 83's aws_public_homeowner_document_sign_capability, which stays as it is. The spec prerequisites stand for SQL 82 and SQL 83: their four functions, homeowner_ledger_tokens, claims, check_intake_items, homeowner_ledger_events, check_endorsements, signature_requests and signature_signers with every column the bodies read or write, pg_catalog.gen_random_uuid() and role checksops; a read-only production inspect confirms them. Each replaced function must be owned by the applying login (functions_owned_by_login), keep its jsonb result (function_results_match) and hold no EXECUTE grant other than PUBLIC, authenticated, checksops and the owner (function_acl_replaceable); the login must be able to write check_endorsements and signature_signers under RLS (definer_can_write_relations). No API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin.Adds no trigger: the DB validator's public trigger count is not affected.

tooling.note: Guarded tooling for SQL 127: sql127-homeowner-portal-signing-production-apply.mjs --inspect (read-only) and the receipt-gated --apply on the engine shared with the staging guarded executor (choice sql127-homeowner-portal-signing); production-sql-one-shot.mjs --migration sql127. intended_replacement_sha256 is the code-derived fingerprint (releaseIntendedHash in release-sql-state.mjs, equal to the staging pin's): the three functions (body and attributes from the file, EXECUTE for checksops and the owner). The tooling does not authorize anything: this pin stays execute false until a reviewed change records the staging acceptance, the production inspect and an owner approval.
